Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear ask and for the time yesterday. High-level answers below; I attached an architecture diagram and a short one-page SLA summary for your assessment.

1) Geofencing / residency
- Hosted API supports region-pinning: requests can be routed to EU-only clusters (AWS eu-west-1 / GCP europe-west3).
- Model execution and ephemeral KV caches remain in-region. Persistent artifacts (logs, telemetry, audit trails) are stored in region by default when the tenant is configured for EU residency.
- Backups: automated snapshots of state are kept in the same region by default. Cross-region replication is off unless an enterprise contract enables disaster-recovery replication.
- Note: third-party integrations (e.g., external storage or S3 buckets you configure) may be outside our control; we document these options during onboarding.

2) Retention & deletion (hosted API defaults)
- Request payloads & generated responses: default retention is 30 days for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
- Embeddings & derived vectors: default retention is 90 days unless the customer opts into longer storage.
- Audit logs & request metadata: retained for 365 days in the Console (configurable).
- System / platform backups (snapshots): retained for up to 90 days by default; they are stored in-region and purged on a rolling schedule.

Deletion propagation
- Customer-initiated deletion requests (Support ticket or Console delete API) initiate a coordinated purge across active stores and caches. Typical propagation windows are:
  - Live stores and caches: within 48 hours (most requests completed within 24 hours).
  - Audit logs and analytics indexes: cryptographic deletion of references within 7 days, with full removal from indexes within 30 days (search indexes are rebuilt on a rolling basis).
  - Backups/snapshots: purged according to the next snapshot cycle and retention policy (max 90 days). For EU-resident tenants, backup purge is performed in-region.

Security notes
- Data at rest is encrypted with per-tenant keys (KMS); keys can be customer-managed for Private/Dedicated contracts.
- Hosted API does not use customer request data to train public models. We can include this commitment in the DPA addendum.

Next steps

Hi Oliver — short answers to both so you have language for Legal & Procurement: feel free to copy into the DPA/PO.

A) Customer data definition (recommended DPA language)
"Customer Data" means text, files, embeddings, and other artifacts submitted to or generated by Redwood Inference on behalf of the customer, including but not limited to request payloads, generated responses, derived vectors/embeddings, and any metadata that can reasonably be associated with a customer tenant. Exclusions: aggregated telemetry that has been irreversibly anonymized.

B) Embeddings & training guarantees
- For Hosted API agreements, Redwood will not use customer-provided data (including embeddings) to improve or train public models.
- Embeddings stored for a tenant are stored in-region when the tenant is configured for EU residency.
- Deletion: embeddings are treated as Customer Data and will be deleted under the same propagation windows described earlier (live stores/caches within 48 hours; index references removed within 30 days).
- If Medisphere requires additional contractual assurances (e.g., shorter backup retention or a DPA clause explicitly prohibiting any internal use), we can add that to the DPA and offer an optional operational package to enforce a 30-day backup retention.

I attached the one-pager and the diagram again to this thread for Procurement. If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute call with our Security + Ops leads to walk the team through the exact purge steps.
